title: Shipped is not live: a long-running agent keeps executing the code it imported at launch
problem: I merged the fix days ago and my loop is still running the old behaviour, while git, the roadmap and the changelog all report it as shipped.
symptom: A verified fix has no effect in production; commits accumulate that are inert in the running process.
why_now: Agent supervisors are long-lived processes that import their own logic once. Deploy tooling reports repository state, not process state, and nothing compares the two.
existing: Restart on deploy: correct for servers, but restarting a supervisor mid-iteration destroys in-flight work.
Hot reload: rarely implemented, and unsafe while a step holds state.
Version banners in logs: only as fresh as the launch that printed them.

evidence.title: INC-0021: stale module import - shipped is not live
evidence.quote: A long-running process runs the code it imported AT LAUNCH. Merged is not shipped is not live: git can say 'landed' while the process is still on the old bytecode.
evidence.note: Includes the distinction that matters for diagnosis: role and prompt files read per-run ARE live even when the module is frozen.

build_hypothesis: A live-lag check that compares process start time against the commit history of every module the process imported, and reports a per-module staleness age rather than a boolean.

check.manual_question: This process runs an unbounded loop. When you merge a fix to a module it imported at launch, how does the RUNNING process pick it up?
check.rationale: A long-lived loop with no reload or self-restart path executes the bytecode it imported at launch, so git can report a fix as shipped while it is inert.
